newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso ends weaker as dollar puts exercised.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso ends weaker as dollar puts exercised.

text.p: The Mexican peso reversed earlier slight gains against the dollar to close marginally weaker on Monday, as brokers exercised dollar puts with the central bank and on forecasts of further cuts in primary interest rates, dealers said.
"The peso zigzagged as some banks oversold dollars in the morning and had to cover shorts in the afternoon," one dealer said.
The benchmark 48-hour peso and its 24-hour stablemate closed 0.2 and 0.3 of a centavo weaker, respectively, at 7.7520/7.7540 and 7.7490/7.7520 per dollar.
"Puts were exercised today. We participated, and we feel the majority did so too," another dealer said.
Banco de Mexico auctioned $300 million in dollar puts on Friday, February 21.

Dealers estimated that the peso also weakened towards the close on expectations that primary interest rates would fall at Tuesday's primary auction and on corporate demand to cover month-end obligations payable in dollars.
"The end of the month is coming and interest rates are still trending downwards," a trader said.
Traders said they expected bellwether 28-day Cetes rates to fall by up to 50 basis points from a current rate of 19.46 percent.
Same-day peso contracts closed 0.45 of a centavo firmer at 7.7420/7.7450 per dollar.
